messages:
incbot: ALERT: increased 95th latency on /v1/generate and elevated CUDA OOMs detected in us-west-2 cluster. paging eng-oncall and eng-runtime :rotating_light:
opsbot: Incident created: INC-3625. Paging on-call (marta) and runtime lead (deepak).
marta (eng-oncall): I'm on it. seeing p95 -> 2.4s -> 12s over last 10m, error rate 3.8%. GPU reclaim logs show multiple processes being killed with `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION` and `OutOfMemoryError`.
deepak (eng-runtime): grabbing logs from the continuous-batcher service. early suspicion: a runaway batch growth + kv-prefetch holding references -> memory spike and then CUDA context faults.
emily (support): got a customer ticket (acct: pelago): "our document summarization jobs saw timeouts and 503s around 20:13 UTC" — high priority. Marking customer-impact P1.
marta (eng-oncall): allocation graph shows a few nodes with queue depth > 30k while typical is < 2k. labeling these nodes as sticky. starting mitigation checklist: 1) disable prefetch on affected pool, 2) reduce batch size cap, 3) drain nodes that show OOMs.
deepak (eng-runtime): +1. pushing `--max-batch-size=128` and `--max-prefetch=0` to the config for pool `us-west-2-batch-small`. applying now.
opsbot: deploy triggered: /deploy config/batcher/us-west-2-batch-small -> canary.
incbot: NOTE: canary started. will monitor 5m for regressions.
kai (eng-sre): I'm seeing kernel logs: repeated page faults and GPU GPU-fault reset entries. node ip 10.2.44.189 had container restarts 4x in 6m. Looks like swapping to host due to mempressure -> I/O thrash.
marta (eng-oncall): can we isolate by routing traffic away from that pool to fallback instances? need to avoid customer impact.
deepak (eng-runtime): routing change in flight: adding routing rule to route requests exceeding 1s to model-compact variant and to dedicated pool with stricter batching.
emily (support): update: Pelago reports partial recovery on their end but still seeing occasional 503s. They asked for ETA.
marta (eng-oncall): ETA: initial mitigations in 5-10m, full stabilization target 45m. telling CS to relay that.
incbot: EVENT: heavy queue-growth traced to continuous-batcher commit a1b2c3 (kv-prefetch refcount change) — suspicion: refcount leak when prefetch fails.
deepak (eng-runtime): I can reproduce locally with stress script: `python tests/stress_prefetch.py --clients 200 --seq 2048` and observing accumulator growth. attaching snippet:
```
> batcher.accumulator.size() -> 42000
> kv_cache.entries_live() -> 51000
> GPU mem -> 95% -> oom
> tracer: prefetch() failed but refcount not decremented in exception path
```

marta (eng-oncall): good repro. escalate to eng-ml for commit revert? we need immediate rollback on prod.
deepak (eng-runtime): rolling back the prefetch change now. creating revert PR and deploying.
opsbot: Rollback job started: config/batcher/us-west-2-batch-small -> rollback to v2026-03-01-4.
kai (eng-sre): while rollback happens, I'm going to cordon the two worst nodes and set `vm.swappiness=10` temporarily, and clear docker's overlay caches. also bumping `oom_score_adj` to favor killing batcher before system.
emily (support): Pelago wants a postmortem and want to know if there's any data loss. any dropped requests?
deepak (eng-runtime): we logged ~1.1k requests that errored with 503s during peak. no tokens lost server-side; these were transient failures. will include in incident report.
marta (eng-oncall): switching to handoff mode in 15m. deepak, can you own the rollback verification and root-cause triage? kai, continue node remediation. I'll coordinate comms and handoff to morning oncall if needed.
incbot: remind: add `incident:high-visibility` tag to INC-3625 and set conference bridge.
opsbot: conference started: zoom.link/INC-3625
deepak (eng-runtime): rollback completed at +12m. canary looks stable: queue depth back to baseline ~1.8k, GPU mem healthy. verifying for 10 more minutes.
kai (eng-sre): nodes cordoned, restarted container runtime, cleared caches. nodes rejoin healthy at +17m.
emily (support): Pelago confirms they no longer see 503s and latency back to normal. thanks team.
marta (eng-oncall): good. summary for handoff: root cause preliminary = refcount leak in kv-prefetch path causing accumulator growth -> memory pressure -> host swapping -> GPU faults and container restarts. mitigations applied: disable prefetch, cap batch size, rollback commit, cordon and remediate nodes, route traffic to model-compact fallback. customer impact: small set of requests (~1.1k) across ~20 customers saw 5xx/timeouts for ~15-20m. follow-ups: postmortem, PR to fix exception-path refcount decrement, add load-shedding in batcher when queue depth > threshold, more aggressive on-host OOM safeguards.
deepak (eng-runtime): adding tests to catch refcount leaks, will open PR today and link to incident.
kai (eng-sre): will add host-level alert for page-fault rates and an auto-evacuate playbook for nodes hitting >3 kernel GPU resets in 5m.
emily (support): sending customer comms now with ETA for full postmortem.
marta (eng-oncall): Handoff: I'm off at +25m. handing to night oncall (kai) for monitoring. if anything spikes, escalate to deepak.
kai (eng-sre): ack. monitoring dashboards set.
opsbot: INC-3625 marked STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring.
incbot: Incident timeline auto-saved. Please add notes to the incident doc. :white_check_mark:
